recent_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

recent_commits.message: Fix repo_check misses for 4TU, Dataverse, Figshare, DSpace7, and DataONE
recent_commits.body:
4TU (#431): .researchdata4tu_id() extracted a DOI-embedded uuid and passed
it straight to v2/articles/<id>, but the API needs a different numeric id
only a live DOI redirect reveals. Added .researchdata4tu_resolve_uuid() to
follow that redirect before querying.

Dataverse (#432): .dataverse_host_from_doi() returned the first host sharing
an ambiguous DOI prefix, picking the wrong DANS Data Station for a shared
prefix (10.17026, used by 4 separate installations). Now resolves via live
DOI redirect when a prefix maps to more than one host; also added the
missing phys-techsciences.datastations.nl prefix entry.

Figshare (#434): added collection-URL/DOI detection
(.figshare_collection_id()/.figshare_collection_articles()), mirroring the
existing project-expansion pattern. Share-links remain correctly flagged as
unsupported (no public API resolves them).

DSpace7/DataONE (#435): dataone_links() missed KNB's real #view/doi: URL
shape and had no fallback for a bare legacy KNB docid (knb.1404.1) cited
with no DOI at all. dspace7_links() had no DOI-based detection whatsoever,
so a paper citing only a DOI (never the host string) was invisible to it --
added live DOI resolution against known DSpace7 hosts.

#433 needed no change: 10.6078 was already added to
.dryad_doi_prefixes() by an earlier commit, before the issue was filed.

All fixes verified live against each issue's reported example. No
regressions in existing archive-dataone/dataverse/dryad/figshare tests.

recent_commits.message: Widen archive-member byte-range retry beyond the fixed 403/429/5xx list (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_bytes() -- the call .zip_member_fetch() makes for both a
member's local header and its compressed data -- only retried a response
matching .storage_is_transient()'s fixed list (403, 429, 500, 502, 503,
504). Any other status (a plain 401, a 400, or anything else not on that
list) was accepted as final after exactly one try, even when the identical
request succeeded moments later on manual reproduction: nothing
distinguishes "this host will never honour ranges" from "that one request
happened to fail" for an unlisted status.

.range_status_is_transient() now retries anything except 200 (host is
deliberately ignoring Range -- a fixed property of the host/URL a retry
cannot change) and 206 (success). Verified against a real, unmocked local
HTTP server that returns 401 once then 206 -- httr2's own retry loop
(req_perform1 -> retry_is_transient(), independent of req_error()'s is_error
override) correctly retries and succeeds on the second attempt.

httr2::local_mocked_responses()/with_mocked_responses() do not exercise
req_retry()'s actual retry loop at all (mock responses return through
handle_resp() before the while(tries < max_tries) loop is reached) -- a
limitation already independently documented elsewhere in this codebase
(test-repo-download.R's skipped "skip_on_api_limit = TRUE gives up on a
confirmed rate limit fast" test). Tests here check the request's configured
retry policy directly instead of trying to simulate multiple attempts
through a mock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Record archive-member download failures in download_repo_files() itself (#429)
recent_commits.body:
The previous commit fixed error propagation inside .zip_fetch_members()/
.zip_member_fetch(), but missed the actual call site the issue reported:
download_repo_files()'s archive-member block (R/repo-download.R) wraps
.zip_fetch_members() in tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL) and, on
any failure -- a thrown error, or a listing that returns NULL, or an
individual member coming back ok = FALSE -- just does `next`, leaving
file_location = NA with nothing recorded anywhere. This is the exact code
quoted in the issue.

Moved `failed`'s initialization earlier (it previously appeared after this
block ran, so there was nowhere to record into) and now populate it for
all three failure shapes, matching the has_url path's existing convention:
the roll-up message() and attr(files, "failed") already downstream pick
these up unchanged.

recent_commits.message: Record why a zip archive-member fetch failed instead of a silent NULL (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.zip_fetch_members()/.zip_member_fetch() collapsed every failure -- a
transient range-request error, a corrupt local header, a CRC mismatch, a
path-traversal rejection, a write failure -- into an indistinguishable
ok = FALSE with no message anywhere, so a corpus-scale run had no way to
tell a retryable failure apart from a host that will never support this.
Each failure path now records a one-line reason, and the five per-provider
download functions (Dryad, Zenodo, Figshare, Dataverse, ReShare) surface it
as a progress message and attach it as a `failed` attribute on the returned
table, matching the convention download_repo_files() already uses.

recent_commits.message: Persist zip_peek() to disk and thread skip_on_api_limit through it (#427)
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek()'s result was cached only in memory (.zip_peek_cache), reset every
R process, unlike repo_info_cache() which already persists a repository's
LISTING to disk for exactly this reason. Added an on-disk cache
(R/zip-peek-cache.R, mirroring repo-info-cache.R's shape: one file per
archive URL, opt-in via cache = TRUE) and wired it into zip_peek(),
zip_decision(), .zip_fetch_members(), and .code_expand_zip(), plus all of
their call sites in repo_check.R, data_check.R, code_check.R, and
repo-download.R.

Also fixed skip_on_api_limit not reaching zip_peek()'s own HTTP helpers:
.head_size(), .http_range_get(), .http_range_tail(), .http_range_suffix(),
.http_range_bytes(), and .range_size() all called .wait_out_known_rate_limit()
and the retry factories with no skip_on_api_limit argument, so a confirmed
exhausted rate limit was always waited out during a zip peek regardless of
what the caller asked for -- the argument only reached them via the global
metacheck.skip_on_api_limit option. repo_check() had no skip_on_api_limit
parameter at all; added one, and data_check()/code_check() now forward their
own skip_on_api_limit both to repo_check() (via module_run()) and to the
zip-peeking step, matching how they already forward cache the same way.

recent_commits.message: Merge pull request #426 from scienceverse/fix-424-zip-peek-s3
recent_commits.body: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts, install-loop variables as packages, empty code files
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts (#424), install-loop variables as packages (#421), empty code files (#425)
recent_commits.body:
#424: zip_peek() on Dryad, Figshare and Harvard Dataverse
- These hosts redirect downloads to Amazon S3, which refuses HEAD (403)
  but honours ranged GETs. When HEAD gives no size, the tail is now
  requested by distance from the end ("bytes=-n") and the total read
  from Content-Range; a 416 answer is handled. The fallback reads the
  status before any body and accepts only 206, so a host that ignores
  the range cannot send a whole archive.
- A size is taken from HEAD only when the answer is 2xx; a 403 on a
  size request is no longer retried.
- .remote_size() falls back to a one-byte ranged GET the same way.
- Removed the OSF, Zenodo and Dataverse whole-archive routes in
  download_repo_files(): those archives never report a size, so the
  routes never ran. Removed .remote_content_length().
- Dryad, GitHub and GitLab archives now follow one rule: size estimated
  from listed file sizes, skipped when unknown or above 2x
  max_download_size, and stopped during download at 2x. GitHub and
  GitLab previously had no limit.
- osf_file_download(mode = "zip"): max_download_size is a budget for the
  whole project. A node whose archive does not fit is downloaded file by
  file within the budget (previously reported as "not downloaded" and
  then downloaded without limit). Partial archives are deleted.
- peek_zips now defaults to TRUE in data_check and reproducibility_check.

#421: dependency extraction
- code_library_names() no longer reports a variable's name as a package
  in install.packages(), requireNamespace(), or library()/require() with
  character.only = TRUE. Variables are resolved to the literal names
  assigned in the file (including for-loop variables, lapply(pkgs,
  library), p_load(char = pkgs)), and dropped otherwise.
- A package install.packages() cannot find is reported with its "not
  available" warning instead of "installed but not loadable".
- A 404 from the CRAN Archive is reported as "not found in the CRAN
  Archive", not as a network failure.

#425: empty code files
- code_abs_path(), code_setwd(), code_install_packages() and
  code_line_stats() handle an empty file without warnings or errors;
  code_parse_r() no longer reads the first line of an empty file.
  code_check previously recorded empty files as errored.

Tests
- New tests for all of the above.
- Existing tests: restore the real zip_peek() after tests that replace
  it; give new download tests their own repository names; add an
  renv.lock to the code_check green-light test (required since 9285b1f).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Convert Grobid TEI to bibr export schema 12.0
recent_commits.body:
grobid_to_bibr(schema_version = "12.0") converts Grobid TEI into a 12.x
paper and saves it as a 12.0 file:

- ids are 1-based positions in document order;
- xref targets come from the xml:id each <ref> points at, for bib,
  figure, table and foot references;
- each caption and footnote is one text row with no section, after the
  body and the reference list, and there are no pseudo-sections; a
  caption starts with its printed label, taken from <head> when figDesc
  leaves it out;
- the source is the PDF next to the TEI (published.pdf for
  published.pdf.tei.xml), else the TEI, so source.sha256 matches a bibr
  export of the same PDF; paper_id is the source's name without its
  extension;
- the producer is Grobid, with the version in the TEI header, and the
  converter is metacheck; completed_at is when Grobid extracted the
  content, from the same header, else the time of the conversion;
- metacheck's own warning codes start with METACHECK_.

The body sentences are made as before. Without schema_version, the
conversion is unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Write bibr export schema 12.0 with paper_write()
recent_commits.body:
paper_write(schema_version = "12.0") saves a paper read from a bibr 12.0
export as a 12.0 file. It keeps the paper's extraction block, so a bibr
export keeps bibr as its producer and bibr's completed_at, and names
metacheck as the converter: rewriting bibr's exports changes nothing but
converter. bib_match rows made by add_bib_match() are converted to the
12.0 columns, and a score that is not on the 0-1 scale is written as null
with a METACHECK_MATCH_SCORE_NOT_0_1 warning. A paper in the older format
is refused, and so is one read from a later 12.x, since its rewrite would
have to keep keys metacheck does not know. Without schema_version,
paper_write() writes what it wrote before.

The tests validate what they write against bibr's strict schema (a copy
in tests/testthat/fixtures/bibr12) when jsonvalidate, now in Suggests, is
installed.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Read bibr export schema 12.x files
recent_commits.body:
.read_bibr() now sends a file with a root schema_version (bibr export
schema 11 and later) to .read_bibr12(), which reads 12.x and stops on any
other version. Files without a root schema_version read exactly as
before. Keys that a later 12.x adds are ignored.

A 12.x paper keeps metacheck's info table, made from metadata and source,
and info_match (metadata_match); the other tables keep their 12.x names
and meanings. Captions and footnotes are text rows with no section that
figure, table and the new footnote table point at with text_id; xref_id
is the row's own key and target_id the row it cites; paper$extraction
holds the export's extraction block. Degrees of freedom stay in
parentheses, as metacheck's statistics code expects.

inst/schema/paper-bibr12.json lists the optional tables and columns this
adds. paper_validate() and .paper_coerce() merge it into paper.json and
skip properties that are not tables (extraction); paper() and paper.json
are unchanged. ref_consistency, ref_miscitation and the table captions of
match_reported_output() read 12.x papers, and ref_accuracy compares the
0-1 match scores of 12.x papers with suggest_score / 100.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Fix .reproducibility_check_batch() hang from callr pipe deadlock (#420)
recent_commits.body:
callr::r_bg() was launched with its default stdout = "|" / stderr = "|",
which pipes a worker's output through a small, fixed-size OS buffer.
Nothing in the polling loop drains those pipes while a worker is still
running, so a paper whose output exceeded the buffer before the parent
read it would block the child on its next write() forever. The process
stays alive (is_alive() == TRUE, CPU frozen rather than accumulating),
so its slot in `running` never frees, the queue never advances past it,
and the dispatcher hangs indefinitely with the remaining queued papers
never launched.

Redirect each worker's stdout/stderr to temp files instead, tracked in
new out_files/err_files lists keyed by pid (the callr process object is
a locked R6 environment and rejects new fields directly). The failure
path now reads the stderr file instead of p$read_all_error(), and both
temp files are removed once a worker's result has been collected.

Verified against a real Docker run (workers = 2, 3 papers): all papers
launch, finish, and combine correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix capture_module_tables() saving modules unnamed (#419)
recent_commits.body:
collect_module_tables() looked up saved modules by name
(j$modules[[module]]), but capture_module_tables() never named the
outputs list, so the lookup always missed and the function silently
returned an empty data frame for every paper. .load_module_tables()
had the same problem via names(saved$modules).

Name outputs from each module's own $module field (read before it is
stripped as plumbing), with a positional fallback for any NA/blank/
duplicate name. Also warn in collect_module_tables() when files exist
but none matched, instead of silently returning empty.

recent_commits.message: Add DataONE and institutional Figshare DOI-prefix coverage
recent_commits.body:
DataONE: added data.piscoweb.org (PISCO, UC Santa Barbara) as a known
member node, and fixed .dataone_pid() not recognising a bare DOI whose
suffix itself contains a further slash (PISCO's own 10.6085/AA/<id>
shape). Both found via a real paper citing this DOI with no host
domain in the URL at all, which dataone_links() could not resolve at
all before this fix.

Figshare: added 28 more institutional instances (found via DataCite's
client registry, searched for "figshare" in the client name) and
Monash University's bridges.monash.edu (found separately, via a real
paper citation, since its DataCite client is named "Monash University"
rather than mentioning Figshare). Taught .figshare_id()/figshare_links()
to recognise each instance's own DOI prefix (e.g. 10.26180 for Monash,
10.25375 for ZivaHub/UCT) when cited as a bare DOI with no host domain
in the URL -- previously only the generic 10.6084/m9.figshare.* DOI
shape was recognised this way, silently missing every institutional
instance's own prefix regardless of how many hosts were already in
.figshare_vanity_hosts(). Also anchored the new id-extraction pattern
on a non-digit boundary rather than end-of-string, since a trailing
sentence period from ordinary prose ("...19095317.v1.") is a common
real-extraction artifact that end-of-string anchoring silently missed.

Every added host confirmed live to answer Figshare's own single-page-app
shell (HTTP 202, non-JSON body) rather than a real API response, the
same discipline the existing 16 vanity hosts use; several DataCite-listed
candidates were checked and excluded because their real platform is
something else entirely (DataverseNO, DTU's Orbit repository, University
of Salford's Worktribe platform).

  outside of the limits is now left out like any other value.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pipe nested calls in tests
recent_commits.body:
* Chains start from a single object and end on the expectation, per the test style in AGENTS.md; no call nests more than two deep, and no pipeline runs inside a call that is itself a pipeline step.
* A chain fits on one line, or, if very long, breaks after every pipe. Consecutive parallel lines stay on one line with their pipes aligned; at the top level, a trailing `# fmt: skip` keeps air from undoing that.
* Replace the `_` placeholder, which needs R >= 4.3, with purrr::pluck(), mapply() with purrr::map2_lgl(), and evalq() with quote() |> eval().
* Keep the call forms that test-vectorize-test.R tests as they are, and leave Allard's reference code in test-grimmer.R verbatim.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Pipe nested calls and pipeline verbs in package code
recent_commits.body:
* Calls nested more than two deep become `|>` chains that start from a single object, with a line break after each pipe.
* dplyr verbs and other pipeline functions are applied through the pipe.
* Tail return() calls are gone; return() is only used for early returns.
* Roxygen examples and vignette chunks follow the same rules.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop leading dots from internal variable names
recent_commits.body:
* Arguments of functions that also take `...` keep their dots, as they guard against clashes with it: those of function_map*(), seq_*_df(), and the functions the two proto factories return.
* The proto factories themselves lose the dotted copies of the formals of the functions they return, which read them from the enclosing environment instead.
* function_map() reserves the renamed locals that could shadow arguments of `.fun`.
* Drop a tail return() in function_map_total_n_proto() and a test helper.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read the string `"NA"` as missing in `restore_zeros()`
recent_commits.body:
* It was reported as a value that is not a number, although it spells
  out a missing one and became `NA` either way.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject non-positive input in `grim_granularity()` and `grim_items()`
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_items(n = 0, gran = 0.05)` returned `Inf` without a word, and a
  negative `n` a negative count. Both now error via `check_positive()`,
  which lets missing values through.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep `unlist()` from coercing list elements in `is_numeric_like()`
recent_commits.body:
* A logical element next to a number became that number, and a factor
  its integer codes, so `list(TRUE, 1)` and `list(1, factor("a"))` were
  numeric-like. A logical value now makes a list `FALSE`, as it does a
  vector, and a factor is tested as its label.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Give 0-row `audit_seq()` output the usual columns
recent_commits.body:
* `*_map_seq()` output records the dispersed variables as the `var`
  element of its `"scrutiny"` attribute. Without rows, `audit_seq()`
  can't read them off the `var` column, and it used to return only
  `hits_total` next to the reconstructed values.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Skip undecidable cases in `*_map_seq()` with `include_consistent`
recent_commits.body:
* A case with a missing key value has no verdict and nothing to disperse
  from. The default path dropped it along with the consistent cases, but
  `include_consistent = TRUE` kept it, and `seq_disperse()` then failed
  on the missing value.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep existing names of a matrix in `row_to_colnames()`
recent_commits.body:
* The name repair replaced every column name with a placeholder, not
  only the missing ones. A column whose header cells are all `NA` keeps
  its current name, so a named matrix lost that name to `V1`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Don't count unused factor levels in `duplicate_count()`
recent_commits.body:
* `table()` counts every level of a factor, so unused levels came out
  with a frequency of 0. Keeping only positive frequencies fixes that and

repos.readme_excerpt:
**Text, section, table and statistic extraction from academic papers (PDF, DOCX, HTML), built
for meta-science.**

docpluck turns a research article into text you can run statistical checks on. It extracts the
text layer, repairs the damage extraction itself causes (lost minus signs, split ligatures,
interleaved columns, Greek letters decoded as Latin), identifies the paper's sections, pulls
tables out as cell grids, flattens table rows into records a statistics checker can read, and
renders the whole paper as Markdown. Every output carries a record of what the library had to
guess or refused

recent_commits.message: fix(render): a trailing bare number moves onto the next heading only when the paper numbers its sections
recent_commits.body:
5a6ab1f moved any trailing single-level "N." past a section's appended
floats, which let the arabic folder glue it onto the next heading. A
125-paper census (2026-10-01, every case checked on the rendered page,
second model concurring) found four headings manufactured that way:
a running page number (10.5334/irsp.945 "43. Discussion", 10.5334/irsp.946
"31. References"), a sentence-final reference digit pulled out of its
sentence (10.1525/collabra.57785 "...in Table" / "8. Discussion") and a
notes item number (10.1177/19485506211056761 "4. Author Contributions").

Multi-level numbers still move on shape (every one in the census was
printed with its heading); components are 1-2 digits with a non-zero first,
so a bare cell value like 0.05 never qualifies. A single-level N moves only
when the document prints a numbered subsection of N or N-1 (10.1017/
jdm.2023.15 keeps "3. Results" now that Table 1 sits between "3." and
"Results"). Census after: the four wrong headings gone, no numbered heading
lost relative to v2.4.147, the multi-level and vouched single-level
restorations kept.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables,render): keep the column labels a caption used to swallow; a float never splits a heading number from its title
recent_commits.body:
Two regressions the full suite found in this branch:

- Header labels deleted. flatten recovers blank column roles from statistic
  labels that leaked into the caption (10.1525/collabra.90203 Table 8
  '... Explicit Learning F p'). 3c8b475 stopped the leak, so when the grid had
  also missed its header row the printed labels reached no field. New Table
  field header_text_below_caption: exactly the span the caption no longer
  absorbs (old trim end vs new), reduced to its leading run of statistic labels
  in flatten's own vocabulary. flatten reads caption + this field, i.e. the
  same input it had before. collabra.90203: T8 'F p', T9 'df F p BF01 95% CI',
  every other table None.
- Heading split. The ligature fix in _locate_caption_anchor lets figures whose
  caption carries a ligature anchor in the body; on 10.1017/jdm.2022.2 Figure 2
  was appended after a section body ending in the next heading's orphan '5.4.',
  so '5.4. Discussion' was no longer rejoined. A trailing bare section number
  now moves after the section's appended floats (nothing removed).

Both tests (test_tables_flatten_blank_header_recovery, orphan multilevel)
fail without these changes and pass with them.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): review fixes -- flatten reads the DOCX declaration from the cells; caption walk robust to raised glyphs and wide spacing
recent_commits.body:
From a tier-2 cross-model review (Sonnet, 2026-09-28) of this branch:

- flatten._declared_header_rows read Table['header_rows'] as the author's
  ceiling. Since 4737846 that field is the POST-fold thead count, so a folded
  second header row went into the body: reproduced on 9 of 415 tables across 66
  real DOCX manuscripts. The declaration is now rebuilt from the cells' is_header
  flags exactly as docx_tables._header_row_count built it; DOCX flatten output
  is identical to v2.4.147 on all 415 tables.
- sync_header_rows: a table with no html and no cells now reports None, not the
  capture path's leftover 1; extract_tables_docx (public) syncs too.
- _column_lines: overlap judged against the smaller of glyph and line height,
  so a raised superscript that opens a line still admits its line's glyphs.
- _caption_text_from_column: lines above the caption are skipped by vertical
  centre (a raised glyph no longer drops the first caption line); the blank
  band is now > 1.2 line heights AND > 1.5x the caption's own smallest gap, so
  double-spaced captions are not cut after one line.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

without this change and passes with it.

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): header_rows states the header split the table's own html used
recent_commits.body:
Each capture path wrote its own guess: Camelot hardcoded 1, the layout path
'1 if any is_header else 0', the DOCX path 'n_header or 1'. The html's <thead>
(and flatten_table, which agrees with it) often used a different number: on
10.1525/collabra.90203 6 of 12 tables disagreed (Table 5: field 0, thead 3).
The field is now set from the html at both structured-extraction exits by
tables.render.sync_header_rows: <thead> row count, 0 when the html has no
header, None when there is no grid. Documented in docs/README.md and on the
Table type.

On the DOCX path flatten._declared_header_rows reads this field as the
author's ceiling; the synced value already had that ceiling applied, so
feeding it back gives the same split.

Owner decision 2026-09-28 (d-756293): make the field honest rather than
document the old guesses. Public field change -> consumer notice.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

recent_commits.message: fix(tables): a table caption stops at its own header row; ligatures and symbol-font glyphs no longer break its anchor
recent_commits.body:
Three causes of one symptom -- caption text that is not the printed caption,
and the table it labels exiled to 'Tables (unlocated in body)':

- A lone statistic symbol on its own line (p, t, d, n, df, or a Greek-led
  symbol such as eta-p2) was read as a wrapped title word because it is
  lowercase, so the cell-run cut never fired. 10.1525/collabra.90203 p12
  Table 8 caption ended '... Explicit Learning F p'.
- The column caption rebuild grouped chars into lines by round(top); a
  symbol-font glyph sits a point or two off its line and became a line of its
  own. 10.1016/j.evolhumbehav.2016.06.001 p4 Table 1 came out as
  'Table 1 alpha Summary ... Cronbach's for ... HKSS. alpha' (the second alpha
  is the header row's). Lines are now grouped by vertical overlap, in one
  helper shared by the caption and column-body walks; a line-end hyphen is
  kept and the break dropped, the library's H1 convention.
- _locate_caption_anchor compared a caption still carrying U+FB01 against the
  normalized body; it now decomposes ligatures with the same function
  normalize used on the body (Hurst Tables 4 and 6).

Hurst: 3 of 6 tables were in the appendix, now 0. Two-sided: 12 new checks
fail on 05fb622 and pass here; 191 existing caption/anchor tests pass.
recent_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

floats, which let the arabic folder glue it onto the next heading. A

  labels that leaked into the caption (10.1525/collabra.90203 Table 8

  also missed its header row the printed labels reached no field. New Table
  field header_text_below_caption: exactly the span the caption no longer
  absorbs (old trim end vs new), reduced to its leading run of statistic labels

  same input it had before. collabra.90203: T8 'F p', T9 'df F p BF01 95% CI',

- Heading split. The ligature fix in _locate_caption_anchor lets figures whose
  caption carries a ligature anchor in the body; on 10.1017/jdm.2022.2 Figure 2
  was appended after a section body ending in the next heading's orphan '5.4.',

_new_commits.message: fix(tables): review fixes -- flatten reads the DOCX declaration from the cells; caption walk robust to raised glyphs and wide spacing
_new_commits.body:
From a tier-2 cross-model review (Sonnet, 2026-09-28) of this branch:

- flatten._declared_header_rows read Table['header_rows'] as the author's
  ceiling. Since 4737846 that field is the POST-fold thead count, so a folded
  second header row went into the body: reproduced on 9 of 415 tables across 66
  real DOCX manuscripts. The declaration is now rebuilt from the cells' is_header
  flags exactly as docx_tables._header_row_count built it; DOCX flatten output
  is identical to v2.4.147 on all 415 tables.
- sync_header_rows: a table with no html and no cells now reports None, not the
  capture path's leftover 1; extract_tables_docx (public) syncs too.
- _column_lines: overlap judged against the smaller of glyph and line height,
  so a raised superscript that opens a line still admits its line's glyphs.
- _caption_text_from_column: lines above the caption are skipped by vertical
  centre (a raised glyph no longer drops the first caption line); the blank
  band is now > 1.2 line heights AND > 1.5x the caption's own smallest gap, so
  double-spaced captions are not cut after one line.
_new_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

after its label, printed alone on its line above a gap and the title. The
rebuild then returned nothing and the text channel interleaved the neighbouring

_new_commits.message: fix(tables): a column-rebuilt caption ends at a blank band it measures itself
_new_commits.body:
The line grouping in 3c8b475 yields only lines with chars in the caption's own
column, so the old 'blank band' stop -- which fired only when the OTHER page
column printed a line inside the gap -- could no longer fire. On
10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901 p5 Table 2 the caption then ran on into its header
row ('... for datasets used Class Class Class Class'). A gap of more than 60%
of a line height between consecutive caption lines now ends the caption.

Found by the 125-paper caption census (v2.4.147 vs branch); the test fails
without this change and passes with it.
_new_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

_new_commits.message: fix(tables): header_rows states the header split the table's own html used
_new_commits.body:
Each capture path wrote its own guess: Camelot hardcoded 1, the layout path
'1 if any is_header else 0', the DOCX path 'n_header or 1'. The html's <thead>
(and flatten_table, which agrees with it) often used a different number: on
10.1525/collabra.90203 6 of 12 tables disagreed (Table 5: field 0, thead 3).
The field is now set from the html at both structured-extraction exits by
tables.render.sync_header_rows: <thead> row count, 0 when the html has no
header, None when there is no grid. Documented in docs/README.md and on the
Table type.

author's ceiling; the synced value already had that ceiling applied, so
feeding it back gives the same split.

Owner decision 2026-09-28 (d-756293): make the field honest rather than
document the old guesses. Public field change -> consumer notice.
_new_commits.author: Gilad Feldman

_new_commits.message: fix(tables): a table caption stops at its own header row; ligatures and symbol-font glyphs no longer break its anchor
_new_commits.body:
Three causes of one symptom -- caption text that is not the printed caption,
and the table it labels exiled to 'Tables (unlocated in body)':

- A lone statistic symbol on its own line (p, t, d, n, df, or a Greek-led
  symbol such as eta-p2) was read as a wrapped title word because it is
  lowercase, so the cell-run cut never fired. 10.1525/collabra.90203 p12
  Table 8 caption ended '... Explicit Learning F p'.
- The column caption rebuild grouped chars into lines by round(top); a
  symbol-font glyph sits a point or two off its line and became a line of its
  own. 10.1016/j.evolhumbehav.2016.06.001 p4 Table 1 came out as
  'Table 1 alpha Summary ... Cronbach's for ... HKSS. alpha' (the second alpha
  is the header row's). Lines are now grouped by vertical overlap, in one
  helper shared by the caption and column-body walks; a line-end hyphen is
  kept and the break dropped, the library's H1 convention.
- _locate_caption_anchor compared a caption still carrying U+FB01 against the
  normalized body; it now decomposes ligatures with the same function
  normalize used on the body (Hurst Tables 4 and 6).

Hurst: 3 of 6 tables were in the appendix, now 0. Two-sided: 12 new checks
fail on 05fb622 and pass here; 191 existing caption/anchor tests pass.

highlights.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
highlights.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

highlights.message: Pipe nested calls in tests
highlights.body:
* Chains start from a single object and end on the expectation, per the test style in AGENTS.md; no call nests more than two deep, and no pipeline runs inside a call that is itself a pipeline step.
* A chain fits on one line, or, if very long, breaks after every pipe. Consecutive parallel lines stay on one line with their pipes aligned; at the top level, a trailing `# fmt: skip` keeps air from undoing that.
* Replace the `_` placeholder, which needs R >= 4.3, with purrr::pluck(), mapply() with purrr::map2_lgl(), and evalq() with quote() |> eval().
* Keep the call forms that test-vectorize-test.R tests as they are, and leave Allard's reference code in test-grimmer.R verbatim.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Pipe nested calls and pipeline verbs in package code
highlights.body:
* Calls nested more than two deep become `|>` chains that start from a single object, with a line break after each pipe.
* dplyr verbs and other pipeline functions are applied through the pipe.
* Tail return() calls are gone; return() is only used for early returns.
* Roxygen examples and vignette chunks follow the same rules.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Drop leading dots from internal variable names
highlights.body:
* Arguments of functions that also take `...` keep their dots, as they guard against clashes with it: those of function_map*(), seq_*_df(), and the functions the two proto factories return.
* The proto factories themselves lose the dotted copies of the formals of the functions they return, which read them from the enclosing environment instead.
* function_map() reserves the renamed locals that could shadow arguments of `.fun`.
* Drop a tail return() in function_map_total_n_proto() and a test helper.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Read the string `"NA"` as missing in `restore_zeros()`
highlights.body:
* It was reported as a value that is not a number, although it spells
  out a missing one and became `NA` either way.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject non-positive input in `grim_granularity()` and `grim_items()`
highlights.body:
* `grim_items(n = 0, gran = 0.05)` returned `Inf` without a word, and a
  negative `n` a negative count. Both now error via `check_positive()`,
  which lets missing values through.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep `unlist()` from coercing list elements in `is_numeric_like()`
highlights.body:
* A logical element next to a number became that number, and a factor
  its integer codes, so `list(TRUE, 1)` and `list(1, factor("a"))` were
  numeric-like. A logical value now makes a list `FALSE`, as it does a
  vector, and a factor is tested as its label.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Give 0-row `audit_seq()` output the usual columns
highlights.body:
* `*_map_seq()` output records the dispersed variables as the `var`
  element of its `"scrutiny"` attribute. Without rows, `audit_seq()`
  can't read them off the `var` column, and it used to return only
  `hits_total` next to the reconstructed values.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Skip undecidable cases in `*_map_seq()` with `include_consistent`
highlights.body:
* A case with a missing key value has no verdict and nothing to disperse
  from. The default path dropped it along with the consistent cases, but
  `include_consistent = TRUE` kept it, and `seq_disperse()` then failed
  on the missing value.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep existing names of a matrix in `row_to_colnames()`
highlights.body:
* The name repair replaced every column name with a placeholder, not
  only the missing ones. A column whose header cells are all `NA` keeps
  its current name, so a named matrix lost that name to `V1`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Don't count unused factor levels in `duplicate_count()`
highlights.body:
* `table()` counts every level of a factor, so unused levels came out
  with a frequency of 0. Keeping only positive frequencies fixes that and
  also covers the ignored values, which the old filter removed.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject an infinite `denominator`; unlist lists in `is_numeric_like()`
highlights.body:
* Both fraction functions share `check_denominator()`, which also rules
  out `Inf`, where `reround_to_fraction()` returned `NaN`.
* `is_numeric_like()` tests a list like the atomic vector of its
  elements, so a logical element is no longer read as a number.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Remove a zero-row branch misplaced into `audit_total_n()`
highlights.body:
* ea7e286 meant it for `audit_seq()` only. In `audit_total_n()`, it
  called `reverse_map_seq()` on total-n output, which fails.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Correct docs of helpers and mappers
highlights.body:
* The `absorb_key_args()` example no longer warns at top level.
* `manage_helper_col()` is called by `function_map()` mappers, not only
  by handwritten ones.
* The mappers take a tibble, and GRIMMER's verdict involves `sd`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Compare `duplicate_count_colpair()` values as strings
highlights.body:
* The other `duplicate_*()` functions compare strings, so the two
  disagreed on values like `0.1 + 0.2` and `0.3`.
* The docs now say that `total_x` and `total_y` exclude ignored values.
* `restore_zeros()` names the non-numbers it turns into `NA`, instead of
  leaking base R's coercion warning.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Align `grim_total()`, `items = NA`, and `reround()` zeros
highlights.body:
* `grim_total()` checks `digits_x` with `check_digits_whole()`, which
  now takes the argument's name for its message.
* `grim()` and `grimmer()` accept a logical `NA` for `items`.
* `reround()` adds zero to its result to drop a negative zero.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix small inaccuracies in `var`, `audit()`, and `grim_plot()`
highlights.body:
* `*_map_seq()` rejects a `var` outside the reported columns, and the
  docs no longer offer `items`.
* DEBIT's `audit()` counts distinct `n` without `NA`; GRIMMER's returns
  zero `fail_*` counts on output without rows.
* `grim_plot()` reads `reason` with `[[`, which doesn't warn.
* Docs of `grim_plot(n)` and `incons_to_prob` now match the code.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep the shape of mapper output at the edges
highlights.body:
* `*_map_seq()` without inconsistent cases returns a 0-row tibble with
  the usual columns, classes, and attribute, which `audit_seq()` and
  `reverse_map_seq()` now accept.
* A data column named like a result column is an error rather than
  being silently dropped.
* `recycle_digits()` attributes its error to the mapper, and
  `check_dispersion_linear()` names the function it was called from.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Convert unnamed matrices quietly in `row_to_colnames()`
highlights.body:
* `tibble::as_tibble()` without `.name_repair` warned about a tibble
  2.0.0 deprecation and told the user to report it to scrutiny.
* An out-of-range `row` is now an error rather than a silent no-op.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject a non-finite `from` in `seq_disperse()`
highlights.body:
* A missing, infinite, or non-numeric `from` has no decimal level. It
  was blamed on `out_min` or failed deep inside `restore_zeros()`.
* The docs now say that the limits don't apply to `from` itself.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Handle empty and missing input in `duplicate_*()` and `grim_items()`
highlights.body:
* `duplicate_count()` builds its counts by hand, since
  `tibble::as_tibble()` fails on an empty table.
* `duplicate_detect()` and `duplicate_tally()` cut the flattened values
  into columns by a factor, which also works with no rows, and name an
  unnamed matrix's columns `col1`, `col2`, ...
* `grim_items()` ignores missing whole-number checks.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Count decimal places of numbers under any `sep`
highlights.body:
* `as.character()` writes a number with a point, which was then searched
  for `sep`. Numeric input now always uses `"."`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Fix `function_map()` argument handling at the edges
highlights.body:
* A custom `.name_key_result` as `.col_names[1]` crashed every call:
  the column already had its final name, and the generated code renamed
  `consistency` anyway. The rename now only runs without `.col_names`,
  which must start with `.name_key_result`.
* `.args_defaults` naming a key or disabled argument, and `.fun` formals
  that the body's locals would shadow, are errors at creation time.
* `check_args_disabled()` reads the caller's dots with `...names()`
  instead of the call, which through `lapply()` names nothing.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Read an `items` column in `*_map_total_n()`
highlights.body:
* The proto function rebuilt the data from the reported columns and `n`
  only, so an `items` column never reached the basic mapper. Helper
  columns are now carried along, one value per case, and un-merged
  afterwards like the `items` argument.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Stop `split_by_parens()` from overwriting existing columns
highlights.body:
* `dplyr::across()` wrote `{col}_{end1}` and `{col}_{end2}` over any
  column of that name, whose original values then replaced the split
  part. This is now an error, as is `end1 == end2`.

highlights.message: fix(tables,render): keep the column labels a caption used to swallow; a float never splits a heading number from its title
highlights.body:
Two regressions the full suite found in this branch:

- Header labels deleted. flatten recovers blank column roles from statistic
  labels that leaked into the caption (10.1525/collabra.90203 Table 8
  '... Explicit Learning F p'). 3c8b475 stopped the leak, so when the grid had
  also missed its header row the printed labels reached no field. New Table
  field header_text_below_caption: exactly the span the caption no longer
  absorbs (old trim end vs new), reduced to its leading run of statistic labels
  in flatten's own vocabulary. flatten reads caption + this field, i.e. the
  same input it had before. collabra.90203: T8 'F p', T9 'df F p BF01 95% CI',
  every other table None.
- Heading split. The ligature fix in _locate_caption_anchor lets figures whose
  caption carries a ligature anchor in the body; on 10.1017/jdm.2022.2 Figure 2
  was appended after a section body ending in the next heading's orphan '5.4.',
  so '5.4. Discussion' was no longer rejoined. A trailing bare section number
  now moves after the section's appended floats (nothing removed).

Both tests (test_tables_flatten_blank_header_recovery, orphan multilevel)
fail without these changes and pass with them.
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: fix(tables): review fixes -- flatten reads the DOCX declaration from the cells; caption walk robust to raised glyphs and wide spacing
highlights.body:
From a tier-2 cross-model review (Sonnet, 2026-09-28) of this branch:

- flatten._declared_header_rows read Table['header_rows'] as the author's
  ceiling. Since 4737846 that field is the POST-fold thead count, so a folded
  second header row went into the body: reproduced on 9 of 415 tables across 66
  real DOCX manuscripts. The declaration is now rebuilt from the cells' is_header
  flags exactly as docx_tables._header_row_count built it; DOCX flatten output
  is identical to v2.4.147 on all 415 tables.
- sync_header_rows: a table with no html and no cells now reports None, not the
  capture path's leftover 1; extract_tables_docx (public) syncs too.
- _column_lines: overlap judged against the smaller of glyph and line height,
  so a raised superscript that opens a line still admits its line's glyphs.
- _caption_text_from_column: lines above the caption are skipped by vertical
  centre (a raised glyph no longer drops the first caption line); the blank
  band is now > 1.2 line heights AND > 1.5x the caption's own smallest gap, so
  double-spaced captions are not cut after one line.
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: fix(tables): a blank gap right after a bare label does not end the caption
highlights.body:
The blank-band stop (previous commit) ended 10.15626/mp.2022.3108 p7 Table 3
after its label, printed alone on its line above a gap and the title. The
rebuild then returned nothing and the text channel interleaved the neighbouring
column: 'Table 3 Table 4 Study stimuli ...'. The stop now skips a gap that
follows label-only text. Found by re-running the caption census; the test fails
without the exemption.
highlights.author: Gilad Feldman

highlights.message: fix(tables): a column-rebuilt caption ends at a blank band it measures itself
highlights.body:
The line grouping in 3c8b475 yields only lines with chars in the caption's own
column, so the old 'blank band' stop -- which fired only when the OTHER page
column printed a line inside the gap -- could no longer fire. On
10.48550/arxiv.2410.21901 p5 Table 2 the caption then ran on into its header
row ('... for datasets used Class Class Class Class'). A gap of more than 60%
of a line height between consecutive caption lines now ends the caption.

Found by the 125-paper caption census (v2.4.147 vs branch); the test fails
without this change and passes with it.
